Vande Mataram.question: What is Vande Mataram? National song of India.
Vande Mataram.fact: "Vande Mātaram" is a poem that was adopted as the national song of the Republic of India in 1950.  It was written in Sanskritised Bengali by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in the 1870s, and was first published in 1882 as part of Chatterjee's Bengali novel Anandmath.  In May 2026, the cabinet headed by Narendra Modi approved a proposal to grant Vande Mataram legal protection under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act in par with the national anthem of India, making disrespect during its rendition punishable by law.  The poem is an ode to the motherland, it was officially adopted by the Indian National Congress in 1905 to serve as a pan-Indian, nationalist salutation to Mother India during the Indian independence movement, culminating in its 1950 designation as the National Song of the Republic of India, sharing equal honour with India's National Anthem.  The first two verses of the song make abstract reference to the "mother" and "motherland", without any religious connotation.  However, later verses mention Hindu goddesses such as Durga

After completing his Bachelor of Arts, he joined the colonial government as a civil servant, becoming a Deputy Collector and later a Deputy Magistrate.  Chatterjee was very interested in recent events in Indian and Bengali history, particularly the Revolt of 1857 and the previous century's Sanyasi Rebellion.  Around the same time, the administration was trying to promote "God Save the King" as the anthem for Indian subjects, which Indian nationalists disliked.  It is generally believed that the concept of "Vande Mataram" came to Chatterjee when he was still a government official, around 1876
